title: Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui
note: Ruler credited with replanning Cusco and starting Inca expansion; chronicle date 1438 versus radiocarbon (Burger et al. 2021; Marsh et al. 2017; Covey et al. 2025) is the core perspective. Link Machu Picchu as his estate.

title: Siege of Cusco by Manco Inca (1536–1537)
note: Only encyclopedias were opened for place-cusco; needs chronicle-based sources (Titu Cusi Yupanqui's account, Pedro Pizarro, the anonymous Relación del sitio del Cuzco) and a scholarly synthesis. Julian dates; Spanish force c. 190–196; Indigenous allies; Saqsaywaman fighting.

title: Neo-Inca state of Vilcabamba (1537–1572)
note: Indigenous resistance state founded by Manco Inca after the failed siege; ends with the capture and execution of Túpac Amaru I in 1572. Sites: Vitcos, Espíritu Pampa.

title: Coricancha (Temple of the Sun) and Santo Domingo convent
note: Sacred core of Inca Cusco, overbuilt by the Dominicans and exposed by the 1950 earthquake. place-cusco could not verify its coordinates or measurements; needs a heritage-register point, wall survey and the ceque system.

title: Pacariqtambo, Puma Orco and Maukallaqta (Inca origin place)
note: Bauer (1991, Latin American Antiquity) identifies Puma Orco as the Tambotoco of the Manco Capac origin myth and Maukallaqta as a possible oracle; the legend should be recorded as belief (confidence legendary).

title: Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II (1780–1781)
note: Largest Indigenous uprising of colonial Spanish America, centred on the Cusco region; include Micaela Bastidas and the execution in Cusco's main plaza (audience_note).
